_about: Side-by-side mode: everything that crosses between the two games each frame (cache/live_pose.bin written by mordhau_side/PoseStream, cache/live_input.txt written by plugin/src/Link.cpp). Exact byte layouts are in the header comment of mordhau_side/PoseStream/Scripts/main.lua. verified = seen working in the running games.

rows.carries: cache/live_pose.bin (131072 bytes (room for 24 stand-ins; the pose block is written up to the places in use, its closing sequence at the fixed end), MORDHAU -> Skyrim) and cache/live_input.mem (16384 bytes, Skyrim -> MORDHAU): fixed size, never truncated or replaced, kept open by both games. live_input.mem: uint32 sequence, uint32 length, the text line, uint32 sequence again.
rows.used_for: shared memory: Skyrim's plugin maps both files (CreateFileMapping / MapViewOfFile) and reads / writes its own memory; MORDHAU's script keeps one Lua file handle on each and writes / reads in place (seek to 0, one write or read). Windows backs the mapping and the handle with the same pages, so nothing is opened, renamed or re-read from disk per frame. A reader takes a block only when the sequence at its start equals the one at its end.

rows.rate: one pose per MORDHAU frame (MORDHAU runs at 200+ frames a second with its picture blacked out), so every Skyrim frame has a new one. Skyrim shows the newest pose as it is: body, weapon and first-person camera all from the same sample. Only a stand-in whose pose arrives slower than Skyrim draws (an idle one among several) is eased between samples.

rows.carries: up to 24 places (Link::kGhosts, the script's MAX_GHOSTS); how many are used is builds.json standin_limit (settings menu, default 12). The first three's states (28 bytes each) sit where they always did, the others follow the player's weapon block; poses in slot order after the state block. The script writes only the places in use and blanks a place once when it is freed (all places on its first write), then the closing sequence number at the block's fixed end; it asks MORDHAU for as many bots as Skyrim sends stand-ins plus two spare

rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-16. 128 = the fixed size of the shared blocks (Link::kGhosts, the script's MAX_GHOSTS); more than Skyrim keeps fully running around the player. 2026-10-16 ~14:08, after a battle with 128: MORDHAU wrote all 128 slots (~570 KB) every pose, its pose rate fell from ~200 to 83 a second and the characters looked like a slideshow; play-testing. Then the limit went into the settings menu with 24 places

rows.carries: Installed by a mod manager (the plugin loaded by SKSE from Data/SKSE/Plugins, MORDHAU's side beside it in Data/SKSE/Plugins/MordhauSkyrim/mordhau): the plugin runs the session. It finds MORDHAU through Steam (or MordhauPath in MordhauSkyrim.ini), puts UE4SS and the PoseStream script into MORDHAU's Binaries/Win64 (only missing or older files of its own; someone's own UE4SS is left alone), writes cache_dir.txt, live_options.lua and live_session.txt, copies the loader in as dwmapi.dll, starts MORDHAU windowed with SteamAppId 629760, takes the loader out as soon as MORDHAU has loaded it (or after 25 s), starts MORDHAU again when it closes, and ties MORDHAU to Skyrim's process (a job object: MORDHAU ends when Skyrim ends, however Skyrim ends). Order: MORDHAU at once when the cache exists, else after the plugin has built it. A MORDHAU that is already running is never touched.
rows.used_for: one ordinary mod: installed by Vortex / Mod Organizer 2, started with the usual play button, no scripts to run
rows.verified_with: copied into Data by hand, Mod Organizer 2.5.2 (virtual folders), Vortex (hardlinks) - 2026-10-10
rows.insecure: play-test note, 2026-10-11. The mod's own MORDHAU (started by the plugin) is always started with -insecure: declared as not for anti-cheat-protected play. Whether MORDHAU acts on the argument is not verified.
rows.launch_race: Another MORDHAU is looked for twice: before anything is done, and again with the loader already in the folder, immediately before the launch. If one has appeared, the loader is taken out again and the launch is put off until it has closed. A MORDHAU that starts in the remaining instant and loads the loader has no session key: the loader ends it and loads nothing.

rows.carries: The script, the moment it runs in a mashup session, renames dwmapi.dll in MORDHAU's Binaries/Win64 to dwmapi.dll.old (a loaded file can be renamed, not deleted). Whoever started the session deletes it later.
rows.used_for: the loader never stays loadable after a session's MORDHAU has started, even if Skyrim dies in that moment

rows.carries: A free stand-in walks MORDHAU's own ground in MORDHAU's walking mode (its AI's own pace). Its BODY (mesh) is shifted up or down against its capsule - through the character's BaseTranslationOffset, which MORDHAU sets the mesh back to every frame - by (player height + Skyrim's height difference) - its own capsule height, eased, at most 60 cm; a held stand-in has no shift. Back in on 2026-10-10  after the rollback; the 'flying' movement mode stays out.
rows.used_for: swings meet the stand-in at the height Skyrim shows, without changing how MORDHAU's AI moves it
rows.verified_how: 2026-10-10 tools/height_test.py, D: copy, Whiterun bridge, 60 samples each: fix on - feet spread 82 cm, pelvis spread 13 cm (std dev 1.7); fix off - feet 96, pelvis 96 (std dev 30). Not yet played by a person.

rows.carries: The plugin, which starts the mod's MORDHAU, makes a random key for that one start, puts it into that MORDHAU's environment as MORDHAU_SKYRIM_SESSION and writes it as the second line of cache/live_session.txt (first line: the time). The script, the moment it loads: no key in its environment, or not the one in the file, or the file older than 10 minutes -> the game is ended at once (os.exit, no asking, no waiting). Every second while running: not a stand-alone local match -> ended. (-insecure is not checked by the script: the command line could not be read from it; it follows from the key, since the only start that has the key always passes -insecure.)
rows.used_for: the script can only run in a MORDHAU the mod started itself, offline, with -insecure - never in one started through Steam for online play, even if the loader was left in the folder (before: a normal start within 10 minutes of a mod session passed the first check, and a failed one took seconds to close)
rows.verified_how: 2026-10-11, D: copy: (1) started by the plugin - key matches, live after 17 s, 0 script errors; (2) loader put into the folder by hand and the game started without a key - the script ended the game at once: the engine's own log closes 2 s after it opened (the process itself was gone from the task list about a minute later).

rows.carries: The loader put into MORDHAU's Binaries/Win64 as dwmapi.dll for a session's start is the mod's own (loader/, built by tools/build_loader.bat), not UE4SS's stock proxy. The moment Windows loads it into Mordhau-Win64-Shipping.exe - before any script host, before the engine starts - it reads the process's own command line and environment from Windows: unless the command line has -insecure AND the environment has MORDHAU_SKYRIM_SESSION (the one-time key, at least 16 characters), it renames its own file to dwmapi.dll.old (so the next start is clean), leaves a one-line note (MordhauSkyrim-closed-MORDHAU.txt) and ends the process with TerminateProcess - no engine shutdown, UE4SS.dll never loaded. Only when both are there does it load UE4SS.dll - and at that same moment it renames its own file to dwmapi.dll.old as well (play-test note, 2026-10-11), so no loadable loader is in the folder from the first instant of a session; the plugin deletes dwmapi.dll.old when MORDHAU has closed, or at the next session's start. In either case it passes every dwmapi call on to Windows' own dwmapi.dll (all 99 exports, by name or ordinal). In any other program it does nothing but pass calls on.
rows.used_for: review note, 2026-10-11: enforce -insecure at the level of the operating system, not by the script alone - the loader itself refuses to load and ends the process with a hard terminate. With the script's exit the process had lingered about a minute.
rows.verified_how: 2026-10-11, D: copy, tools/loader_test.py: no -insecure and no key / -insecure without key / key without -insecure - process gone after 0.04-0.08 s each, UE4SS never started, loader renamed, note written. Normal session through the plugin: live after 19 s, 0 script errors, only dwmapi.dll.old in the folder during the session. Not verified: on another PC; under an antivirus.

rows.carries: Every frame the script asks the engine whether the game is still a stand-alone local match. The frame it is not: (1) the script stops everything it does - no input applied, no stand-ins driven, no pose written (PS_stopped); (2) it writes cache/live_stop.txt with the reason; (3) it asks MORDHAU to quit and calls the hard exit with no grace period. The plugin looks for live_stop.txt five times a second: it ends MORDHAU's process with TerminateProcess, waits until the process is really gone and logs how long that took from the signal; then deletes the file. The plugin also deletes a stale live_stop.txt before every start.
rows.used_for: play-test note, 2026-10-11: immediate response when a session stops being offline - before: checked once a second, then a three-second grace period, and the script's own exit left the process around (~1 min seen at start-up).
rows.verified_how: 2026-10-11, D: copy, mid-fight, PS_testNotAlone forced three times (tools/stop_test.py, timed on the process handle): the script's last pose 31-34 ms after the trigger was handed over; MORDHAU's process gone after 1014 / 792 / 993 ms. Plugin log: signal seen after ~140 ms, process gone 755-989 ms after the signal. A real server join was not used as the trigger.
rows.unknown_state: If the engine's answer is not a clear yes (the call fails, or returns anything but true / false) the state is UNKNOWN: the script does nothing that frame (no input applied, no stand-ins driven, no pose written), and after one second of unknown it stops as for 'not offline'. It never assumes offline.
rows.unverified_boundary: UNVERIFIED INTEGRATION BOUNDARY (play-test note, 2026-10-11). The whole runtime check rests on one engine query, KismetSystemLibrary:IsStandalone, asked from the player controller's tick. Verified: the shutdown path once the script believes the state is 'not offline' or 'unknown' (forced by test switches). NOT verified, and deliberately not tested with a real online transition: (a) that every way a session can stop being local - joining by server browser, by Steam invite, by console, hosting a listen server, a seamless or a hard map travel - makes that query answer false or fail; (b) that the script's frame keeps running through such a transition (it is driven by the controller's tick; during a level change there may be no controller, and the outer loop has ended by then); (c) how early in a connection attempt the answer changes - a handshake with a server may precede it. What does not depend on this boundary: the loader's launch check, -insecure on the mod's own MORDHAU, and that MORDHAU's window takes no meaningful input (observed by play-testing, cause unknown).

rows.carries: The plugin reads the sequence number of cache/live_pose.bin five times a second, on its own thread (independent of Skyrim's frames and loading screens). Armed once the session has been live. No new data: tolerated up to stall_seconds; from unverified_seconds on the session is logged as UNVERIFIED (not as safe) and MORDHAU's window is put back if it was minimised (a minimised MORDHAU stops its frames); at stall_seconds MORDHAU's process is ended from outside (TerminateProcess, waited for) and started again offline like after any exit. Data arriving again before that ends the stall and is logged with its length.
rows.used_for: play-test note, 2026-10-11 The explicit unsafe states (not offline, unknown: offline_stop) stay immediate and are the script's own; this is for a script that has stopped reporting at all.
rows.verified_how: 2026-10-11, D: copy, mid-fight (tools/stall_test.py): whole process frozen 3 s and 12 s - survived, the 12 s one logged UNVERIFIED, the fight went on; script silenced with the game running - ended by the plugin after 31.2 s (process gone 948 ms after the kill), then restarted. Not tested: a Skyrim loading screen of over 30 s with MORDHAU minimised.

rows.carries: ' gw:<id>,<right>,<forward>,<cm>,<margin cm>' per walked stand-in that has a wall near its body: the wall's normal (pointing away from the wall) in the player's frame (right, forward; as g:'s place), the distance from the body to the wall in cm, and how far short of it to keep the stand-in
rows.used_for: the script pushes a free stand-in back out to that line in MORDHAU, so it does not walk into a wall its Skyrim body cannot pass (sheets/builds.json standin_wall_reach)

rows.carries: a stand-in's pose: only the bones the Skyrim body is posed from are read each pose - the mordhau_bone and dir_mordhau_bone of every row of sheets/bone_map.json and every bone above them up to the root (found once with GetParentBone); the rest stay zero (not streamed: the plugin takes their rest pose); fingers as before every 45th pose. The player's own pose is read in full as before
rows.used_for: fewer calls into MORDHAU per pose (measured 2026-10-17: 25 of the 28 body bones - I had guessed about 80; it saves next to nothing, the pose rate's cost lies elsewhere): a higher pose rate with many stand-ins. Only for Skyrim bodies (sheets/builds.json skyrim_bodies 1); MORDHAU-drawn stand-ins would need the rest
rows.source: play-test note, 2026-10-17 (item 5, first part: read only the bones the Skyrim body uses)
